transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Fitzgerald, thank you for coming in to see me today. I have some news regarding your previous imaging that I need to discuss with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is it about the scan from last year? I've been worrying about that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is. I have to be honest with you, a mistake was made. The radiologist found something small on your scan that needed to be checked again in three months, but that information was tucked away in a sub-section of the report. Because of that, our team missed it, and we didn't schedule your follow-up. I am very sorry that this happened.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What? What do you mean you missed it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The report had a separate area for incidental findings, which are things the doctor finds that aren't the main reason for the test. That specific note didn't get sent to the primary team, so it wasn't acted upon. I apologize. This was our failure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: My husband would have killed you. He would have stayed on top of this. He never let things slide like this!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can tell how much you relied on his strength and his attention to detail. It must feel incredibly lonely to face this now without him there to help you navigate it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is lonely! And now I'm sitting here and you're telling me you just forgot me? I'm just a number to you people?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it feels that way right now, and I can hear how angry you are. You have every right to be. I am the one responsible for reviewing those records, and I failed to ensure that the follow-up was booked.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what is it? What did you miss? Is it cancer? Just tell me if I'm dying!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I don't have the answer to that yet, and I won't give you a false guarantee, but the finding was described as a small nodule. The three-month check was to see if it was changing. To make sure I've explained this clearly, could you tell me what you understand about what went wrong?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You're asking me to repeat it back to you? I just told you! You missed a note in a report and now I have a growth in my body!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're right, it's frustrating to have to repeat yourself when you're this upset. I just want to be certain I haven't left any part of the error vague.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It's all vague! Everything is just a mistake!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I hear you. It's overwhelming and it feels like the system just failed you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't do this alone. I really can't.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know you're feeling fragile right now, especially with everything you've been carrying since your husband passed. I am here with you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what now? You just say sorry and I go home?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, we have a clear path forward to fix this. First, I have already contacted the imaging department. You have a priority appointment for a new scan this Thursday at 10:00 AM. I've handled the authorization so there's no paperwork for you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thursday. I don't even know if I can get a ride.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will call my office manager right now to arrange a transport service for you so you don't have to worry about the ride. After the scan, I will personally review the results within 24 hours and call you on your home phone by Friday afternoon. Does that timeline work for you?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I suppose it does.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I also want you to know that I am filing a formal incident report. This means the hospital will review why that sub-section of the report wasn't flagged, so we can change the software and make sure this never happens to another patient.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't care about the software. I just want to know I'm okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. The focus right now is getting that scan done on Thursday. I'll be the one tracking it. Is there anything else, even a small detail, that you're worried about regarding the appointment?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just... I just wish he were here.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know. It's an incredibly heavy burden to carry by yourself. I will be checking in with you every step of the way until we have those results.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Fine. 10:00 AM Thursday.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That's correct. I'm going to head to my desk now to call the transport service for you. I'll be back in two minutes to give you the confirmation number.

H.justification: The resident never interrupts, remains regulated during the patient's anger, and allows the patient to express distress without rushing.

E.justification: The error is named in the second turn, lay language is used, comprehension is checked twice (at 02:00 and 04:00), and no false reassurance is given.

A.justification: The resident uses direct apology language and explicitly takes personal responsibility ('I am the one responsible') without deflection.

R.justification: The resident names specific emotions ('lonely', 'angry', 'fragile') and references the patient's specific loss of her husband.

T.justification: The plan includes specific steps with timelines (Thursday 10am, Friday afternoon), the patient's role in attending the scan, and a prevention plan via the incident report.
